title: Small tracking notebook
text: In this jupyter notebook we will see how to use OpenCV to track an object in a video. We’ll first select the object (Region Of Interest) then track it through the frame and finally we’ ll plot the evolution of the barycenter of the object with regard to the frame number.

title: Small tracking notebook
text:
Import the used libraries
We’ll need

OpenCV (cv2)
tracking_tools to read the ROI
matplotlib to do our plots
IPython.display for the inline display of the tracked video in the notebook



Code
import cv2
from IPython.display import display, clear_output
import numpy as np
import tracking_tools as tt
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

title: Small tracking notebook
section: Choose the video file and select the ROI
text:
Choose the video file and select the ROI


Code
video_path  = "Resources/Pendulum/pend.mov"  
bbox        = tt.select_ROI(video_path)


Select a ROI and then press SPACE or ENTER button!
Cancel the selection process by pressing c button!

title: Small tracking notebook
text:
Initialise the tracker
The tracker is the CSRT tracker from OpenCV based on (Lukezic et al. 2017) that we initialised based of the bounding box surrounding delimiting the ROI.


Code
cap         = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
flag, frame = cap.read()

if hasattr(cv2, 'legacy'):
    tracker = cv2.legacy.TrackerCSRT_create()
else:
    tracker = cv2.TrackerCSRT_create()

tracker.init(frame, bbox)
positions   = []
frame_num   = 0

title: Small tracking notebook
text:
Actual tracking
We now loop over the frame to perform the actual tracking and store the positino of the barycenter of the ROI for each frame.


Code
while True:
    frame_num +=1
    flag_read, frame = cap.read()
    if not flag_read:
        break
    flag_track, bbox = tracker.update(frame)
    if flag_track:
        x, y, w, h  = [int(v) for v in bbox]
        center_x    = x + w // 2
        center_y    = y + h // 2
        positions.append([frame_num, center_x, center_y])

        cv2.rectangle(frame, (x, y), (x + w, y + h), (245, 70, 58), 2)
        cv2.circle(frame, (center_x, center_y), int(0.1*min(h,w)), (245, 70, 58), -1)
        cv2.putText(frame, f"({center_x},{center_y})", (20, 40),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (245, 70, 58), 2)
    else:
        cv2.putText(frame, "Lost", (20, 40),
                    cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (247, 59, 218), 2)

    rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)  

    clear_output(wait=True)
    plt.imshow(rgb)
    plt.axis('off')
    plt.show()

cap.release()

title: Small tracking notebook
text:
Post-processing


Code
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook_connected"
positions = np.array(positions) 

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=positions[:,0],  
    y=positions[:,1],  
    mode='lines',
    name='X',
    line=dict(color='rgb(58,70,245)')
))

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=positions[:,0],  
    y=positions[:,2],  
    mode='lines',
    name='Y',
    line=dict(color='rgb(23,15,48)')
))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Position over time",
    plot_bgcolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)',  # Remove background color
    xaxis_title="Frame number",
    yaxis_title="Position (pixels)",
    legend=dict(x=0, y=1),
    width=900,   
    height=500,  
)

fig.show()

title: Tracking objects with OpenCV
text:
Welcome!

In this demo we will see how to use OpenCV to track an object in a video. We’ll first select the object (Region Of Interest) then track it through the frame and finally we’ ll plot the evolution of the barycenter of the object with regard to the frame number.
The notebooks can be executed online with binder  (no download required).

To run the notebook locally you’ll need to setup an environment with opencv, matplotlib and numpy. Follow these steps to create a Conda environment named tracking-ev with Python 3.13 and all required packages:
# Create a new conda environment with Python 3.13
conda create -n tracking-env python=3.13 -y

# Activate the environment
conda activate tracking-env

# Install required packages: OpenCV (with contrib modules), NumPy, and Matplotlib
conda install -c conda-forge opencv=4.8.0 matplotlib numpy -y
